title: 10. Profit and Loss, Discount and Tax

q.t: CP = ₹400 and SP = ₹460. Find the profit percent.
q.e: Profit = 60, measured on the cost price: 60/400 = 15%.

q.t: Marked price = ₹500 and discount = 10%. Find the selling price (in ₹).
Discount is equal to:
q.e: A discount is the amount taken off the price printed on the tag.

q.t: CP = ₹250 and the loss is 20%. Find the SP (in ₹).
Find a 25% discount on a marked price of ₹800 (in ₹).
SP = ₹1200 and the profit is 20%. Find the CP (in ₹).
An article is priced at ₹600 and 5% tax is added. Find the bill amount (in ₹).
Discount percent is always calculated on the:
q.e: The discount is offered on the price shown to the customer — the marked (list) price.

q.t: CP = ₹80 and SP = ₹100. Find the profit percent.
q.e: Profit 20 on a cost of 80: 20/80 = 25% (not 20% — the base is CP).

q.t: Marked price = ₹1000 and SP = ₹850. Find the discount percent.
q.e: Discount = 150 on a marked price of 1000 = 15%.

q.t: Marked price = ₹1600 and discount = 15%. Find the SP (in ₹).
After a 15% discount an article sells for ₹2040. Find the marked price (in ₹).
Successive discounts of 20% and 10% are given on ₹1000. Find the final price (in ₹).
q.e: 1000 → 800 (20% off) → 720 (10% off 800). The second discount applies to the reduced price, so it is not 30% in all.

q.t: An article costing ₹1500 is marked 20% above cost and sold at a 10% discount. Find the profit percent.
A bill of ₹2240 includes 12% tax. Find the price before tax (in ₹).
The cost price of 12 articles equals the selling price of 15. Find the loss percent.
q.e: Let each cost ₹1. 15 articles cost ₹15 but sell for ₹12: loss 3 on 15 = 20%.

q.t: A grocer mixes 80 kg of rice at ₹13.50 per kg with 120 kg at ₹16 per kg and sells the mixture at ₹18 per kg. Find his gain percent.
An article is sold for ₹4800 at a loss of 4%. Find the CP (in ₹).
After a discount of 12.5% an article sells for ₹1750. Find the marked price (in ₹).
q.e: 12.5% = 1/8, so the SP is 7/8 of the marked price: 1750 × 8/7 = 2000.

q.t: What single discount equals successive discounts of 10% and 10%?
A trader marks goods 40% above cost and gives a 25% discount. Find his profit percent.
A dealer gives a 10% discount and still gains 20%. The article cost him ₹600. Find the marked price (in ₹).
q.e: SP = 120% of 600 = 720, which is 90% of the marked price: 720 ÷ 0.9 = 800.

q.t: Successive discounts of 20% and x% equal a single discount of 28%. Find x.
An article is sold at a loss of 12%. If it had sold for ₹60 more, there would have been a gain of 8%. Find the CP (in ₹).
q.e: From −12% to +8% is 20% of CP = 60, so CP = 300.

q.t: List price ₹2500, discount 10%, then 8% tax on the discounted price. Find the amount paid (in ₹).
Two articles are sold for ₹1955 each, one at a gain of 15% and the other at a loss of 15%. Find the overall loss percent.
By selling 33 m of cloth a merchant gains the selling price of 11 m. Find his gain percent.
q.e: Take SP as ₹1 per metre: SP = 33, gain = 11, so CP = 22. Gain % = 11/22 = 50%.

q.t: A machine is bought for ₹3000, ₹600 is spent on repairs, and it is sold for ₹4500. Find the gain percent.
CP = ₹1250 and the required gain is 16%. Find the SP (in ₹).
An article marked ₹250 is sold at a 16% discount, and the seller still makes a 5% profit. Find the CP (in ₹).
Goods are marked 50% above cost, then given successive discounts of 20% and 10%. Find the profit percent.
A retailer buys goods at a 20% discount on the list price of ₹5000 and sells them at the list price. Find his profit percent.
q.e: He pays 4000 and sells for 5000: profit 1000 on 4000 = 25% (the base is his cost, not the list price).

q.t: A sells to B at a 10% profit, and B sells to C at a 5% loss. C pays ₹1672. What did A pay (in ₹)?
A dishonest dealer sells at cost price but uses a 900 g weight for 1 kg. Find his gain percent.
q.e: He gives 900 g but is paid for 1000 g. Gain = 100 g on the 900 g he actually parts with: 100/900 = 11 1/9%.

q.t: A customer pays ₹1320 including 10% tax. The shopkeeper’s profit is 20%. Find the shopkeeper’s cost price (in ₹).
q.e: Price before tax = 1320 ÷ 1.1 = 1200. That is 120% of cost, so CP = 1000.

q.t: An article sold at a 20% discount gives a profit of 12%. What would the profit percent be with no discount?
q.e: 0.8 × MP = 1.12 × CP, so MP = 1.4 × CP. Selling at MP gives 40% profit.

q.t: Two horses cost ₹16,000 altogether. They are sold for the same price, one at a gain of 20% and the other at a loss of 20%. Find the total loss (in ₹).
q.e: If each sells for s, the costs are s/1.2 and s/0.8, totalling 25s/12 = 16,000, so s = 7680. Total SP = 15,360: a loss of 640.

q.t: ‘Buy 3, get 1 free’ is the same as a discount of what percent?
q.e: You take 4 items but pay for 3 — one out of four is free: 1/4 = 25%.

q.t: A profit of 20% reckoned on the SELLING price is what percent of the cost price?
q.e: If SP = 100, profit = 20 and CP = 80. On the cost price: 20/80 = 25%.

q.t: An article costs ₹1000. The trader wants a 17% profit after giving a 10% discount. What should the marked price be (in ₹)?
q.e: He needs SP = 1170, which must be 90% of the marked price: 1170 ÷ 0.9 = 1300.
